index_5day_move:DOW.narrative: Broad-market and cyclical names have lagged over the past week as rising Treasury yields and oil prices weigh on rate-sensitive and industrial stocks more than mega-cap tech. A hot core CPI print (+0.3% m/m vs +0.2% forecast) raised the odds of a Fed hike at the Sept 15-16 FOMC meeting from ~70% to ~90%, and Iran's attacks on commercial/naval vessels in the Middle East have pushed oil higher, adding an inflation and cost headwind for industrials and consumer names that make up a larger share of the Dow than the Nasdaq.

citations.title: Global Bond Selloff Sends 10-Year Treasury Yields to Cusp of 5%
Markets Begin Cautiously as Rising Crude and Geopolitical Tensions Persist

index_5day_move:DOW.reaction_assessment: proportionate - move is consistent with the rate/inflation/oil narrative, not a surprise dislocation

index_5day_move:RUSSELL2000.narrative: Small caps are more rate-sensitive than large caps (higher average leverage, more floating-rate debt), so the run-up in the 10yr yield toward 5% on hot inflation data and hawkish Fed signaling has hit the Russell 2000 harder than large-cap indices over the past week. The same Middle East-driven oil spike also raises input costs disproportionately for smaller, less diversified companies.

citations.title: Treasury yields face 4.8% test as fiscal risks threaten to spill into other assets

index_5day_move:RUSSELL2000.reaction_assessment: proportionate - small-cap rate sensitivity is a well-known mechanism, not an anomaly

yield_move:DGS10.narrative: The 10-year Treasury yield's 12bp jump is the mechanical center of this week's story: a hotter-than-expected core CPI print (+0.3% m/m) pushed the market-implied odds of a Fed rate hike at the Sept 15-16 FOMC from ~70% to ~90%, and a global bond selloff (fiscal deficit concerns, heavy Treasury issuance) is compounding the move. Yields are now at their highest level since 2023, approaching the highest since 2007.

citations.title: Global Bond Selloff Sends 10-Year Treasury Yields to Cusp of 5%
10 year treasury yield leaps to 3 week high on promising economic data

yield_move:DGS10.reaction_assessment: proportionate but notable - this is the single biggest macro driver of the week, with a live FOMC meeting (Sept 15-16) as the next catalyst

oil_move:DCOILWTICO.narrative: WTI crude's jump reflects Middle East supply fears after Iran's attacks on commercial and U.S. Navy vessels, which the Iranian Foreign Ministry has framed as retaliatory. Brent has held above $90/bbl. Higher oil adds to the inflation picture the Fed is already responding to, reinforcing (not just coinciding with) this week's yield move.

citations.title: Markets Begin Cautiously as Rising Crude and Geopolitical Tensions Persist
Stock Market Update: Futures Flat, Oil Prices Soar Amid Geopolitical Tensions

oil_move:DCOILWTICO.reaction_assessment: proportionate - directly tied to an active, escalating geopolitical conflict, not a one-off spike

HPE.narrative: HPE jumped 12% after a record fiscal Q3 (revenue $12.2B, +34% y/y) and raised FY26 guidance (EPS $3.75-$3.85, revenue growth 34-37%), driven by a $3.5B hyperscaler inferencing deal and an expanded Oracle AI data center collaboration. Part of a broader enterprise-AI-infrastructure rally that also lifted DELL, NTAP, VICR and ON the same week.

citations.title: HPE Surges As Record Q3 And Oracle AI Deals Reset Outlook

DELL.narrative: Dell surged on a blowout fiscal Q2 FY27: record $47B revenue (+58% y/y), EPS +273% y/y, and a record $60.9B in AI server orders leaving a $95B backlog. Stock is up 230%+ YTD and just joined the S&P 100. Multiple banks (RBC, Morgan Stanley, Goldman, Citi) raised price targets after the print.

citations.title: Dell stock surges on record orders for AI servers

VICR.narrative: Vicor jumped 10% after announcing a major U.S. fab capacity expansion (Merrimack + Hooksett, NH, ~1M sq ft combined) to meet AI power-delivery demand, alongside a 145% y/y backlog surge and a new $150M buyback. Real capacity commitment, not just sentiment.

citations.title: Vicor Stock Climbs with Backlog Up 145%, More Capacity Coming

NTAP.narrative: NetApp's strongest Q1 in company history: revenue $2.03B (+30% y/y) vs ~$1.84B expected, EPS $2.58 vs $2.12 consensus, billings +36%. All-flash arrays (+47%) and Public Cloud (+28%) both accelerating on AI workload adoption. Argus raised its price target to $225.

citations.title: NetApp NTAP Stock Jumps After Blowout Q1 And Raised 2027 Outlook

ON.narrative: ON Semiconductor's 8.5% move was mostly sector beta - a broad chip-stock rally rather than name-specific news - though Q2 revenue ($1.60B, +9.2% y/y) beat consensus and Q3 guidance came in above expectations on AI-data-center power-chip demand. Stock remains 24% below its June record high.

citations.title: ON Semiconductor Stock Jumped Nearly 9% in a Day

LEU.narrative: Centrus Energy's drop is technical, not thesis-breaking: the company priced a $500M stock-and-warrants offering, and new-share dilution mechanically pressures price. Third straight down day (-8.6% Friday alone). Nuclear-fuel demand thesis is unaffected by this financing event.

citations.title: Centrus Energy (LEU) Stock Trades Down, Here Is Why

QLYS.narrative: Qualys fell alongside a sector-wide cybersecurity selloff (profit-taking after a late-August rally, some insider-sale disclosures) rather than new company-specific bad news. Q2 beat estimates; Q3 guidance of 9-10% revenue growth is healthy but didn't support the post-earnings valuation run-up.

citations.title: Qualys (NASDAQ:QLYS) Stock Price Down 3.9% - Time to Sell?

KAI.narrative: Kadant's decline reflects a broader industrial-sector rotation (oil above $100, rising yields) plus a multi-year CEO succession announcement creating near-term uncertainty - not a results problem. The company just beat consensus EPS ($3.42 vs $2.94) and revenue estimates.

citations.title: Why Kadant (KAI) Shares Are Trading Lower Today

DOCN.narrative: DigitalOcean's decline is a valuation reset despite strong fundamentals (a 73% earnings surprise still triggered an 11% post-earnings drop) - the concerning part is $570.5M of insider selling over the past 12 months with zero insider buying, on a still cash-flow-negative business. Worth watching, not a clean bounce case.

citations.title: DigitalOcean Holdings Inc (DOCN) Shares Fall 3.5% -- What GF Score of 67 Tells Investors

RCUS.narrative: Arcus Biosciences' drop reflects genuine fundamental deterioration, not overreaction: the company scrapped its Phase 3 STAR-121 and Phase 2 EDGE-Lung trials for domvanalimab after a futility analysis showed no survival benefit, while H1 2026 revenue collapsed to $58M from $188M and net loss widened to $219M.

citations.title: Arcus Biosciences Stock Stumbles After Harsh Double Blow

GWRE.thesis: Guidewire fell 20.6% on Sept 4 despite beating Q2 revenue (+15.3% y/y) and EPS estimates - the selloff was triggered by FY27 guidance implying ARR growth decelerating from 19% to ~18% and Q3 revenue guided 3.3% below consensus. A one-point deceleration in an otherwise-healthy growth story looks like an overreaction; bounce thesis rests on ARR growth staying in the high teens, not collapsing.

citations.title: Guidewire Software (GWRE) Is Down 21.1% After Tempered Fiscal 2027 Outlook Despite Solid ARR Trends

TBBK.thesis: CAUTION - this one likely fails the bounce screen's "no fundamental deterioration" test and is flagged rather than a clean recommendation: the 21% drop followed Chime's agreement to acquire Stride Bank for $590M, meaning Chime plans to move its banking relationship away from The Bancorp entirely once that deal closes (H1 2027). This is a real, structural loss of a key partner's transaction volume and fee revenue - not noise. Include with reduced conviction pending clarity on how much of TBBK's book Chime represents.

citations.title: Why Is The Bancorp Stock Down 21% Today?

PATH.thesis: UiPath is down ~25% from its late-August high after Q2 CY26 results missed the high bar set for AI-linked names; management cited macro variability and shifts in customer adoption patterns. Real but modest headwind - agentic/RPA automation demand is still growing, this reads more like multiple compression on a still-early AI-software category than a broken thesis.

citations.title: Dips In UiPath Stock Have Mostly Kept Falling, Will This One Too?

COO.thesis: Cooper Companies fell 13.9% after Q4 guidance ($1.05-$1.09 EPS) missed the $1.19 consensus and management decided not to sell CooperSurgical after a strategic review - the market wanted a divestiture and didn't get one. Contact-lens distributor inventory drawdown is a real near-term drag but not a demand problem; bounce thesis depends on inventory normalizing in FY27.

citations.title: Why is CooperCompanies Stock Down 15% Today?

CASY.thesis: Casey's beat both revenue and earnings estimates for the quarter, yet fell 18% on decelerating same-store sales growth (3.2% vs 4.3% prior year) and a fuel-margin tailwind management flagged as temporary. Classic "beat but guide cautious" overreaction pattern in a still-profitable, cash-generative convenience-store operator.

citations.title: Why Did Casey's General Stores Stock Tank This Week?

CSGP.thesis: CoStar is down ~68% from its 52-week high despite revenue still growing 21% with a 79% gross margin - the market has re-rated the stock hard on competitive/execution concerns (its residential push against Zillow) rather than a revenue collapse. Classic value setup if the core commercial real estate data business keeps compounding while the market has priced in near-failure of the residential bet.

citations.title: CoStar Group (NASDAQ:CSGP) Sets New 52-Week Low - Time to Sell?

KTOS.thesis: Kratos is down 37% YTD despite a strong defense backlog and hypersonics revenue guided to ~$400M in 2026 and $700M+ in 2027 (MACH-TB program funding), plus recent $20M and $35M contract wins. Value case: the stock's multiple has compressed even as the forward revenue/earnings trajectory improved.

citations.title: Kratos Defense & Security Solutions, Inc. (KTOS) Stock Price & News - Google Finance

FISV.thesis: Fiserv is down 64% over the past year after slashing 2026 guidance to roughly flat organic revenue, driven partly by Argentina inflation normalization. Real fundamental deterioration, not pure sentiment - but at 72% below one fair-value estimate ($48.65 vs $174.38 GuruFocus GF Value), this is a case where the market may have overcorrected for a genuine but bounded problem.

citations.title: Fiserv stock tumbles after cutting 2026 guidance

BSX.thesis: Boston Scientific is down ~60% from its September 2025 all-time high after a cyberattack disruption and slowing electrophysiology/WATCHMAN growth forced a guidance cut to 6.5-8% organic growth. Real operational hit, but the growth-rate cut (not a growth reversal) at a much lower valuation ahead of an Oct 28 earnings report is the value setup here.

citations.title: Has BSX Stock Fallen Far Enough To Buy?

DUOL.thesis: Duolingo is down 41% YTD after management deliberately chose user growth over near-term monetization (guiding 2026 bookings growth to ~11% vs the ~20% it could have delivered under the old approach). This is a valuation reset (14.6x forward P/E vs a 3-year average of 88x), not a demand problem - the growth-first bet either pays off in re-accelerated bookings later, or it doesn't.

citations.title: Duolingo Stock Is Down 41% in 2026. Here's Why Investors Are Repricing Growth

KHC.thesis: Kraft Heinz's volume pickup looks more technical than thematic: the stock is simply transferring its exchange listing to the NYSE (effective Sept 14) alongside a routine $0.40 quarterly dividend declaration. No fresh operational catalyst - a 6.54% dividend yield makes it a income-oriented hold rather than a high-conviction momentum name. Lower-conviction pick in this bucket.

citations.title: Kraft Heinz to Transfer Stock Exchange Listing to NYSE

RH.thesis: RH beat Q2 FY26 revenue estimates ($922.2M vs $915.4M expected) on strong demand for its new higher-price-point RH Estates collection, and Telsey raised its price target to $155. Real momentum, though Q3 guidance came in below expectations and the Estates rollout to galleries slipped a few weeks - a partial offset worth watching, not disqualifying.

citations.title: Telsey raises Restoration Hardware stock price target on better results

SPSC.thesis: SPS Commerce jumped up to 15.8% on reports that private equity firm GTCR is in advanced talks to acquire the company, which had confirmed exploring a sale back in June. GuruFocus estimates the stock is worth $182.49 versus its $80.90 price - a real, event-driven catalyst with a clear (if binary) path to realizing that gap.

citations.title: Why SPS Commerce Rallied on Friday

MTN.thesis: CAUTION - Vail Resorts' volume spike is momentum without a clean bullish story: free cash flow worsened to -$28.2M (-133% y/y) in Q3, pass sales growth decelerated to +1% (second straight year of declining unit pass sales), and Goldman Sachs initiated coverage with a Sell rating on Aug 17. Include with reduced conviction pending the Sept 28 fiscal Q4/year-end earnings report.

citations.title: Vail Resorts Announces Fiscal 2026 Fourth Quarter and Year-End Earnings Release Date

AEO.thesis: American Eagle beat Q2 revenue and EPS estimates (sales +7.5% y/y) but still fell 15.8% on a 1% comp-sales decline at the namesake brand, with Barclays and Telsey cutting price targets. The volume/momentum signal here is actually a post-earnings selloff, not a rally - flagging as a speculative name to watch for stabilization rather than a clean momentum long.

citations.title: American Eagle (NYSE:AEO) Exceeds Q2 CY2026 Expectations But Stock Drops 12.1%
